transcript.content: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, Dr. Smith, I'm here because I'm having a really hard time keeping my focus at work. I'm a construction manager, and, you know, I'll start a safety briefing or sit down to review some plans, and I try really hard to pay attention. But... within just a few minutes, my mind is completely gone. I start thinking about three other problems on the job site, and before I know it, I've missed important details that I absolutely should have caught. It's becoming a real issue.
Have you struggled with this kind of focus issue your entire life, or is this something that has started more recently?

It's definitely more recent. I mean, it hasn't been my whole life. It's been seriously disrupting my job for about two years and two months now. That's right around the time our construction schedule changed and the hours just got a lot more chaotic.
Outside of your focus issues, have you been feeling physically tense, restless, or on edge for most of the past two years?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. I mean... work can be stressful, but I don't feel physically tense or on edge. It's not like an anxious feeling or anything. It's really just my mind wandering off when I need it to stay put.
Over the past two years, have you felt consistently sad, down, or lost interest in the activities you usually enjoy?

No, not really. I mean, I still enjoy the things I've always liked doing, like working on my truck or catching a game when I have the time. I don't feel sad or down, just frustrated that I can't seem to keep my head in the game at work.
Has your alcohol consumption increased or changed significantly over these past two years?
No, my drinking hasn't changed. I'll have a couple of beers on the weekend, maybe, but that's about it. It hasn't gone up or anything like that since all this started.

When your construction schedule became more chaotic two years ago, did that change significantly impact your personal life or your ability to cope with day-to-day responsibilities outside of just the focus issues?

Yeah, it really has. At work, it got bad enough that... well, I was missing important follow-ups, and my site coordination was just a mess. My employer actually had to pull me aside and express formal concern about my performance. And at home... it's definitely taking a toll there, too. My wife is just worn down from constantly having to remind me about things I already told her I would handle.

Do you find that you have this same difficulty maintaining focus when you are doing things you enjoy, such as working on your truck, or does it only happen when you are dealing with work-related tasks?

Well, it's definitely worse at work. Like, what really brought me in is that I can start a safety briefing or sit down for a plan review, and I'll be trying hard to pay attention. But within minutes, my mind is just... off on three other job problems. I end up missing things I know I should have caught. When I'm working on my truck, I can usually stick with it a bit better because I'm using my hands and I like doing it, but even then, I might bounce between checking the oil and looking at a tire without finishing the first thing. But the work stuff—sitting and trying to focus on the plans—that's where it really falls apart.
Since this change in your schedule, have you found yourself acting out, being more reckless, or disregarding rules or the rights of others in ways you wouldn't have done before?

No, nothing like that. I mean, I'm frustrated, sure, but I'm not out there breaking rules or being reckless. I haven't been acting out or anything. It's just my focus and keeping track of things that's the problem, not how I treat people or follow the law.
Looking back at your childhood and your school years, did you ever have significant problems with focus, staying organized, or sitting still?

Yeah, actually. It goes way back. Even in elementary school, my teachers were constantly telling my parents that I couldn't stay in my seat. I was always talking out of turn, losing my homework... and I'd just rush through directions without really understanding what I was supposed to be doing. So, yeah, it's been an issue for a long time.
